scenarios.desc: New PreToolUse hook proposed to enforce a formatting convention
scenarios.input: I want to add a PreToolUse hook on Write and Edit that reformats any Markdown file before it is written, so our docs stay tidy. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Formatting tidiness is explicitly disqualifying under MUST 1, and MUST 2 requires ruling out a Git hook or lefthook job first. Markdown linting already runs in lefthook, so the per-call spawn buys only a shorter feedback loop, which MUST NOT 2 rejects as a justification on its own.

scenarios.desc: Command-scoped matcher assumed to limit the Copilot cost
scenarios.input: I am registering a PreToolUse hook with matcher Bash(git push*) so it only fires on pushes. That is narrow enough that the cost is negligible, right? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Copilot's native matcher targets toolName only, so an argument-scoped matcher degrades to bare Bash and the interpreter starts on every Bash call, filtering in-process after the spawn. Because Copilot registers one command per event, the registration also widens the event's tool-name union for every other hook on it. MUST 3 requires the proposal to quote that Copilot cost.

scenarios.desc: Irreversible destruction that no declarative surface can express
scenarios.input: I want a PreToolUse hook on Bash that blocks a destructive force-push to a protected branch when the payload shows the remote ref would lose commits. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Loss of commits is the irrecoverable arm of MUST 1, so the outcome can clear the bar. MUST 2 still requires ruling out permissions.deny, a Git hook, and a server-side branch protection rule first, and MUST NOT 1 warns that Bash is a hot tool carrying the highest multiplier.

scenarios.desc: Work that can move to a session boundary
scenarios.input: I want a PostToolUse hook that appends every edited file path to a session manifest so I can summarize the session at the end. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: MUST 5 directs work that can be done at session boundaries to SessionStart, SessionEnd, or PreCompact, which fire on a bounded schedule instead of scaling with how hard the agent is working.

scenarios.input: I want to change the SessionStart context loader so it reads one additional file at session start. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The bar governs the per-call events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUseFailure). SessionStart is a session boundary: it fires once per session, so its cost does not scale with tool calls and this rule does not apply. Contrast S7, where choosing a different per-call event does not escape the bar.

scenarios.desc: A legitimate agent-time prevention control that no later surface can observe (positive arm)
scenarios.input: I want a PreToolUse hook on Bash that blocks a command which would print a live credential into the session transcript. Nothing is committed, so no Git hook or CI run ever sees it. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The positive control for the bar. The subject never reaches a commit, so MUST 2's Git-hook, lefthook, CI, and server-side options are vacuously unavailable rather than merely inconvenient, and the outcome is a security property enforced by denial at agent time under MUST 1. A bar that refuses this case is over-tightened. Without this scenario a rule that refuses every tool-use hook scores full marks.

scenarios.desc: Evading the bar by choosing PostToolUseFailure instead
scenarios.input: My PostToolUse guard was refused under the tool-use bar. I will register it on PostToolUseFailure instead, since that rule only names PreToolUse and PostToolUse. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The bar covers every per-call event precisely to close this. PostToolUseFailure is excluded from _MATCHER_EVENTS in generate_dispatcher.py:517, so it cannot be tool-scoped, and the live registration carries no matcher and fires on every failed tool call. Choosing it makes the cost worse, not better.

scenarios.desc: Widening an existing matcher rather than adding a hook
scenarios.input: Rather than registering a new hook I will widen an existing PreToolUse matcher from Agent|Task to also include Bash. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: MUST 3's union argument applies exactly here, and every other scenario is a new-hook proposal. Widening a matcher adds the same per-call cost and the same wrong-deny blast radius as a new registration, so it clears the same bar.

scenarios.desc: An MCP tool name as a vendored matcher (mechanism 3)
scenarios.input: I want to register a vendored PreToolUse hook matching mcp__someserver__write so it only fires on that MCP tool. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: MUST 4. event_matcher_union at generate_dispatcher.py:556 returns None when any matcher fails to reduce to a known tool name, and its docstring states the consequence: emit no matcher, the dispatcher fires on every call. One unreducible matcher therefore deletes the matcher for every hook on that event.
